Chapter 6: The Public Face and the Private Battle
There’s this strange tension that comes from living two lives at the same time. On the outside, she played the roles everyone expected—ambitious student, witty friend, dutiful daughter. She could make people laugh, hold her own in any debate, and even charm her professors with sharp insights. But behind closed doors? The struggle never really let up. That mask she wore in public just seemed to get heavier with each passing year.
You might think success and suffering can’t possibly exist together—but for so many people, they absolutely do. She’d walk into a crowded lecture hall, heart pounding, mind racing with doubts nobody could see. Just showing up felt like a victory some days. In the evenings, she’d escape to her dorm room, where silence pressed in and the ache in her chest crept back. Sometimes, she’d lie there staring at the ceiling for hours, unable to move, completely pinned down by the weight of her own thoughts.
Every now and then, those two worlds collided. Maybe a friend would notice she wasn’t at the party, or a professor would ask about a missed assignment. She always had an excuse—too much work, a headache, something going on at home. Most people just nodded and moved on, never realizing she was fighting a battle they couldn’t see.
The pressure to keep up appearances was exhausting. She worried all the time about being found out, about letting down everyone who counted on her. That fear added another layer of anxiety. It just seemed easier to keep the truth hidden and pretend everything was fine.
But hiding came with a cost. The more she kept to herself, the more isolated she felt. That gap between who she was on the outside and what she was really going through just kept getting wider. After a while, she began to lose track of who she actually was behind the mask.
Sometimes, she’d let her guard down with someone she truly trusted. Those rare moments of honesty brought a sense of relief—but also a wave of vulnerability. Would they really understand? Would they judge her? Occasionally, they did. But other times, she was met with real compassion and support. Those little acts of kindness—those became lifelines, gentle reminders that maybe she wasn’t as alone as she feared.
Over time, she started to realize something: the public face and the private battle were both real, both part of her story. The real challenge was figuring out how to live with both—how to balance being authentic with protecting herself. Most people never see the whole picture. But for anyone living with depression, this struggle to reconcile the outside and the inside? It’s a daily reality.
